blocks.text: Mercaptans are added to give odour to natural gas. Some thiols have pleasant odours at high dilution: thioterpineol is the key ingredient in the aroma of grapefruit, and cis-glabanum oxathiane is a fragrant compound used in fine fragrances, soaps, shampoos and shower gels. Many naturally occurring odorants are produced synthetically and are also used as flavouring agents.

blocks.prompt: Why are mercaptans added to natural gas, which is itself odourless?
blocks.explanation: Methane has no smell, so a leak could go unnoticed; a trace of a strongly smelling thiol lets people detect a leak by nose long before the gas reaches a dangerous concentration.

items: Mercaptans odorise natural gas; thioterpineol gives grapefruit its aroma; oxathiane is used in fine fragrances; many odorants are made synthetically and used as flavourings.
